title: Usage Scribe and Contract Fallback Orchestrator
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a lightweight 'scribe' layer in the console telemetry pipeline that performs fast, probabilistic contract checks, selective enrichment, and orchestrates a graceful fallback path when strict schema validation would cause large-scale rejections. Goals: 1) reduce tail latency from heavy validation by doing a quick sampled pass in the API plane; 2) provide a soft-reject mode that routes suspicious or evolving payloads to a validation queue + enrichment workers instead of dropping them; 3) emit clear audit events and metrics for every fallback so product and SRE can reason about frequency and root cause. This ticket covers design, implementation, and rollout for the service component that sits between the API gateway and the canonical event-ingest brokers (Kafka).
implementation_notes: Architecture: lightweight Go microservice (scribe) deployed as a sidecar / small pod group in the console backend cluster. It performs: - header-based routing and client hints sampling - stateless fast-contract checks using a compact WASM rule set (precompiled) - checksum-based dedup on hot paths - enrichers (geo/ip, customer metadata) in fallback worker pool - outgoing canonicalization to topic: events.canonical and events.fallback. Backpressure: if fallback queue saturates, scribe will dynamically sample down non-critical events and mark headers for downstream tracing. Observability: distributed tracing tags, per-tenant fallback counters, histogram of validation latency, sample payload storage to s3 with TTL. Security: KMS for payload blobs, ensure no PII persists in sample store. Performance target: add <= 6ms median latency to happy-path; fallback path can be higher but documented.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Scribe deployed in canary region and processes 100% of traffic from a single internal org without lost events. 2) Happy-path contract check (fast-pass) latency median < 6ms, p99 < 25ms. 3) Fallback queue is observable with per-tenant metrics, and no more than 0.2% of events go to fallback in steady-state. 4) End-to-end provenance trace for any event that went to fallback with link to sample in S3. 5) Automated e2e tests that assert canonicalization rules and de-dup behavior.
work_breakdown: Design compact contract DSL and WASM runtime integration
Implement scribe service skeleton, sampling and header tagging
Build fast-contract check pipeline and local rule cache
Fallback worker: enrichment, canonicalization, and retry logic
Metrics and tracing instrumentation + dashboard in Console
Canary rollout plan and throttled global rollout
E2E test harness and load test scenarios
Security review and S3 retention policy for payload samples

notes_for_release: Feature gated behind console.telemetry.scribe flag. Default off for GA; enable for internal orgs during canary. Documented in console release notes and runbook. E2E tests added to infra CI.
investigation_findings: WASM approach is a good tradeoff: compact rule authoring and fast cold-start when cached. Main risk: enrichment worker cost under high fallback rates. Mitigation: conservative sampling + circuit breaker + autoscale.
